heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P handles Overture TPU 95A out of the box with its direct-drive toolhead, achieving dependable print speeds up to 54 mm/s within a 4.5 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. No hardened nozzle or enclosure upgrades are required, though the filament must be fed directly from an external spool rather than the AMS.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with PVP glue stick (applied as a release agent to prevent surface damage)
slicerTweaks: Cap Maximum Volumetric Speed at 4.5 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent extruder slipping and backpressure buckling.
Enable 'Avoid crossing walls' and configure a 1.5mm wipe distance to eliminate stringing tails across exterior boundaries.
Set retraction length to 0.6mm at 30 mm/s with 'Wipe while retracting' checked to manage TPU viscoelastic elasticity.
Lower external perimeter print speeds to 40 mm/s and first layer speed to 25 mm/s to ensure uniform surface finish and consistent bed laydown.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder gear jamming and filament buckling
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive print speeds or attempting to feed TPU through the AMS unit.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Bypass the AMS entirely to feed directly from the external holder, and ensure the maximum volumetric speed does not exceed 4.5 mm³/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Persistent fine stringing and surface pitting
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption in hygroscopic TPU filament vaporizing in the melt zone.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in an active filament dryer at 50-55°C for 6-8 hours before printing, and drop nozzle temperature by 5°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Build plate tearing upon part removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Direct chemical bonding of molten TPU to clean PEI coating.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Coat the build plate with a thin, even layer of glue stick or liquid release agent before heating the bed to 50°C.

faq.question: Can I feed Overture TPU 95A through the Bambu AMS unit?
faq.answer: No. Flexible filaments will compress and snag in the long PTFE tubes and AMS feeder mechanisms; always load TPU using the external rear spool mount.

faq.question: Does the open-frame design of the P1P cause warping when printing TPU?
faq.answer: No. TPU 95A has low thermal shrinkage and benefits from the open-frame airflow, which prevents premature heat creep in the extruder.

faq.question: Why is the speed limited to 54 mm/s on a high-speed printer?
faq.answer: TPU has low melt viscosity and elastic compliance, meaning volumetric flow rates above 4.5 mm³/s (54 mm/s at 0.2mm layer height) cause buckling and underextrusion.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade to a hardened steel nozzle to print Overture TPU?
faq.answer: No. Overture TPU 95A is non-abrasive, making the stock P1P stainless steel nozzle fully compatible without excessive wear.
